But before you make your decision, think twice, the movie is based on a beautiful book and a true story. More than once I’ve used a direct quote from the book to memorialize my own or another’s special doggo. There is a lot to love here, esp the book. Also, I really just enjoy the movie- hilarious and poignant, so yeah, you can end the movie early (i don’t know if I’d suffer thru the ending again) and consider being brave and reading the author’s thoughts in the book. They are truly lovely.

In response to Thackerybinx, yes, this is so not the movie to watch if you have just lost your dog. I wish someone would have warned you. And in response to znancy7, I agree with you, if you are a dog lover and are an empathetic person, skip the ending of this movie. I am so sorry your sister made you watch the whole thing. I have it on DVD and I watched it in the theater, yet my animal loving heart can’t handle watching the end of this movie. I knew what would happen in the end thankfully beforehand, so when I saw it in the movie theater, I walked out right when Marley started showing signs of it getting harder for him to move around. I waited for my friend in the general seating area of the theater, and everyone exited that movie in tears. When I watched it in the theater I had lost my first dog not long before, and there was no way I was going to watch that part. Then, our black lab (my second dog) passed in January of 2018 and my boyfriend wanted to watch it and I skipped it altogether that time. I know I will never watch the ending of this movie. It will bring back all those triggers of losing my dogs.

I sobbed for the last 45 minutes of this movie. I was expecting an uplifting film about a precocious puppy growing into adulthood. I lost one of my dogs just a week before watching this film for solace. Wrong film! Wasn't sleeping to begin with, but made it so much more painful. Anyone who has lost a pet doesn't need that agonizingly dragged out in a film.
Definitely one of the saddest movies I’ve ever watched. I was bawling by the end of the movie.

The tragic end of the real Marley and the film's Marley are slightly different.  What is important is that it was not a gratuitous death, illness happens. Not every outcome is perfect.  

Marley's death, and the grieving by his family  IS NORMAL  and was handled well.  

Go, but be prepared to discuss death of a pet afterwards.

Marley ends up getting a twisted stomach, and her owners have to make the unfortunate decision to euthanize her. Marley dies peacefully in the vet. If you want to skip this part, turn it off when Marley begins having trouble going down the steps.

Marley is suffering from a twisted stomach, and the owner has to make the decision to euthanize Marley.  Very stressful. Brought back bad memories and the fear and grief of making those decisions myself.  The agony drags on.  First Marley gets better, then worse.  No one with empathy should watch this movie or ask a dog-lover to watch it.  I would have turned it off at the first sign Marley was sick, but my sister made me watch it.
